title: Prefix sums
short: Precompute running totals so any range sum is one subtraction.
what: Walk the list once and write down the running total at each point. After that, the sum of any stretch is the total at its end minus the total just before its start. Building costs one pass; every question after that is instant.
analogy: A car's odometer. To know how far you drove between two towns, you don't re-drive the road: you subtract the reading at the first town from the reading at the second.

frames.label: running totals
frames.say: nums is 3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9. We will answer many range-sum questions, so build running totals first.

frames.label: running totals
frames.say: Start the totals at 0, before any number. Then 0 + 3 = 3: each total is the one before plus the number above it.

frames.label: running totals
frames.say: Done in one pass. The last total, 23, is the sum of everything.

frames.label: running totals
frames.say: Sum of 1, 4, 1, 5? Total up to the 5 is 14. Total before the 1 is 3. 14 - 3 = 11, no loop.

frames.label: running totals
frames.say: Sum of 4, 1, 5, 9? 23 - 4 = 19. Every range question is one subtraction: O(1).

when: Many questions about the sum of a range
Count subarrays that add up to k (with a dict of totals)
Balance point where left sum equals right sum
The list does not change between questions
python:
from itertools import accumulate

nums = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9]
prefix = [0] + list(accumulate(nums))
print(prefix)

def range_sum(l, r):          # nums[l] through nums[r]
    return prefix[r + 1] - prefix[l]

print(range_sum(1, 4))
print(range_sum(2, 5))
watch: The leading 0 makes prefix one longer than nums. Sum of nums[l..r] is prefix[r + 1] - prefix[l].
If the list changes often, you must rebuild the totals.
With negative numbers, sliding windows break but prefix sums still work.
